name: 2one DLS knowledge graph
description: Semantic decision graph for the 2one Design System. Two layers: derived (parsed from source) and authored (graph/decisions.json — intents, rules, preferences). Nodes carry an ontology class + provenance; edges carry provenance + decision priority. Reason over it with scripts/graph-decide.mjs. Generated by scripts/build-graph.mjs.

nodes.label: Accessible label
nodes.description: Inputs and controls must have a programmatic label.

nodes.label: APCA + WCAG contrast
nodes.description: Text/UI pairs must clear their APCA Lc threshold, audited light and dark.

nodes.label: Focus management
nodes.description: Overlays must trap and restore focus.

nodes.label: Keyboard operable
nodes.description: All interactive controls must be reachable and operable by keyboard.

nodes.label: Never signal state by colour alone
nodes.description: State must carry an icon, label, or shape in addition to colour.

nodes.label: Reduced-motion support
nodes.description: Animation must respect prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Scrim behind text over media
nodes.description: Never place text directly over media — lay a scrim behind it.

nodes.label: Visible focus indicator
nodes.description: A focusable control must show a focus ring (Lc 15 non-text floor).

nodes.label: Mission
nodes.value: To create structure in an unstructured world.

nodes.label: Confirmation flow
nodes.description: A step that gates an action behind explicit confirmation.

nodes.label: Desktop / md+
nodes.description: Viewport at the md breakpoint and above.

nodes.label: Mobile
nodes.description: Below md; useIsMobile() is true.

nodes.label: Web
nodes.description: Any browser context.

nodes.label: Authenticate
nodes.description: Sign in or sign up.

nodes.label: Confirm an action
nodes.description: Ask the user to confirm before proceeding.

nodes.label: Destructive action
nodes.description: An action that deletes or irreversibly changes data.

nodes.label: Convey essential information
nodes.description: Information the user MUST perceive to succeed (required, error, or instruction).

nodes.label: Low-emphasis action
nodes.description: A secondary/tertiary action that must not compete with the primary.

nodes.label: Navigate
nodes.description: Move between views or destinations.

nodes.label: Primary action
nodes.description: The single most important action in a view or section.

nodes.label: Recover from an error
nodes.description: Understand and fix an invalid input.

nodes.label: Select an option
nodes.description: Choose one or more values from a set.

nodes.label: Submit a form
nodes.description: Send the data the user has entered.

nodes.label: Show supplementary info
nodes.description: Reveal optional, non-essential helper information.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.description: Sign-in / sign-up composed from Card + Label + Input + Button.

nodes.label: Destructive confirmation
nodes.description: AlertDialog gating a destructive action, confirmed by a destructive button.

nodes.label: Form submission
nodes.description: Label + Input + validation message, one primary submit.

nodes.label: Mobile side panel
nodes.description: A panel that renders inline on md+ and as a Sheet on mobile.

nodes.label: Build from the library — never hand-roll parallel chrome
nodes.statement: Compose real 2one components. Never hand-roll a parallel sidebar, card, badge, or 'stage' box for something the library already provides.
nodes.rationale: Parallel chrome is the #1 source of inconsistency and responsive/a11y bugs.

nodes.label: Content pages: header + breadcrumb, not the app menu
nodes.statement: A content/reading page (an explainer, an article) uses a simple header with a clickable logo and a breadcrumb back to the dashboard — not the full app sidebar. Every page has an obvious way home.
nodes.rationale: The app menu on a reading page is noise; a breadcrumb + logo is the clearer, product-standard way back (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §22).

nodes.label: Destructive actions confirm + use the destructive variant
nodes.statement: An irreversible action must use the destructive button variant AND require confirmation via AlertDialog before it runs.
nodes.rationale: Undo-less loss demands a deliberate second step and an unmistakable colour.

nodes.label: Destructive styling requires destructive intent
nodes.statement: Reserve destructive styling (the danger colour) for actions that delete or irreversibly change data. Never use destructive styling for ordinary navigation or non-destructive actions.
nodes.rationale: Destructive colour is a warning; spending it on navigation trains users to ignore it and misreads risk.

nodes.label: Empty collections render an Empty state
nodes.statement: A collection with no items renders the Empty component (icon + message + primary next action) — not a blank area.
nodes.rationale: A blank region reads as a bug; an empty state tells the user what to do next.

nodes.label: Form errors are programmatically associated
nodes.statement: A field error must set aria-invalid and link its message with aria-describedby, and show icon+text (see no-color-alone).
nodes.rationale: Screen readers only announce errors that are wired to the control.

nodes.label: Filters offer Select all + Deselect all
nodes.statement: Any multi-select filter (a set of toggleable options that includes/excludes items) must provide Select all and Deselect all (or Clear) controls, so the whole set can be reset in one action instead of toggling every option by hand.
nodes.rationale: Toggling a long filter option-by-option to include everything or start from empty is slow and error-prone; a bulk Select all / Deselect all is the expected, faster affordance and keeps every 2one filter consistent.

nodes.label: Brand marks need a FIXED ground
nodes.statement: Demo the logo on a fixed ground (bg-white / bg-neutral-950), never a theme token. In-app marks must be theme-adaptive (.dark swap or currentColor).
nodes.rationale: The white logo on bg-foreground vanishes in dark (foreground flips near-white).

nodes.label: Visible focus on every interactive element
nodes.statement: Every interactive element must show a clear focus-visible ring (via the --ring token). Never remove the outline without an equal-or-better replacement.
nodes.rationale: Keyboard users navigate by the focus ring; removing it strands them.

nodes.label: Grayscale only — no brand hue
nodes.statement: Theme the whole system in grayscale. There is no brand hue; the only chromatic tokens are danger and success.
nodes.rationale: The hue-free constraint is what makes every 2one screen read as one system and keeps recolour/theming deterministic.

nodes.label: Reading a @theme token at runtime? Keep it alive
nodes.statement: Tailwind v4 tree-shakes unused ramp vars. If you read var(--color-<ramp>-<step>) at runtime, safelist the ramp utilities; otherwise prefer the always-live semantic tokens.
nodes.rationale: An un-referenced ramp var is absent from :root and paints blank.

nodes.label: Async work shows a loading state
nodes.statement: An async action shows a loading state (Spinner in the trigger; Skeleton for content) and disables re-entry — never a dead click.
nodes.rationale: Silent latency reads as a broken UI and causes double-submits.

nodes.label: Logo: never recolour/rotate/distort
nodes.statement: Never recolour, rotate, stretch, or distort the logo. Use the provided black/white marks on their intended grounds.
nodes.rationale: A modified mark stops being the brand.

nodes.label: Icons: lucide only
nodes.statement: Use lucide-react for every icon. Do not mix a second icon set.
nodes.rationale: One icon library keeps weight, stroke, and metaphor consistent.

nodes.label: Prefer a Sheet over a Dialog on mobile
nodes.statement: On mobile (useIsMobile), present a Dialog's content as a Sheet. Render the trigger at every width; switch the presentation, not the availability.
nodes.rationale: A desktop-sized Dialog is cramped or unreachable on mobile; the Sheet is the reachable equivalent (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §19).

nodes.label: Monospace is for code, not chrome
nodes.statement: Use the mono font only for code blocks and literal commands/paths. Product chrome, labels and prose use the UI font (Inter/Satoshi).
nodes.rationale: Monospace in chrome reads as a developer sampler, not a product, and undercuts the SaaS feel (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §21).

nodes.label: Dark is not invert-and-ship
nodes.statement: Audit every rendered surface×text pair in BOTH themes and keep component colours token-driven so the audit matches the render.
nodes.rationale: A component that hardcodes text-white passes the token audit while rendering unreadable.

nodes.label: Never convey state by colour alone
nodes.statement: State (error, success, selected, active) must be carried by an icon and/or text — never colour alone. An invalid field needs an icon plus a message, not just a red border.
nodes.rationale: Colour-only state is invisible to colour-blind and low-vision users; it is a brand AND accessibility rule.

nodes.label: UI counts and lists are generated, not hand-typed
nodes.statement: Any count, badge number, or list shown in the UI derives from the generated source (manifest.json / graph.json) — never a hand-typed literal.
nodes.rationale: Hand-typed numbers drift the moment the repo grows — a nav badge read 198 while the graph held 213. Deriving from source keeps the UI honest by construction (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §20).

nodes.label: One container language — every panel is a real Card
nodes.statement: Every panel is a real Card — same border, radius, padding, shadow. Do not invent bespoke boxes, and do not nest a Card in a Card.
nodes.rationale: One container language is what makes screens feel like one product.

nodes.label: One primary action per view
nodes.statement: Each view/major section has exactly one primary (filled) action. Everything else is outline/ghost/secondary.
nodes.rationale: Competing primaries destroy the visual hierarchy that tells users what to do.

nodes.label: One 8px spacing scale
nodes.statement: Use the 8px spacing scale via Tailwind utilities (gap-4, p-6, mt-6). No ad-hoc inline margins or off-scale pixel values.
nodes.rationale: Inconsistent gaps are the single most visible 'AI-generated' tell.

nodes.label: One system across every surface — even bespoke ones
nodes.statement: Every surface shares the logo, fonts, tokens and theme — including surfaces that cannot be a component shell (e.g. a data-viz canvas). A page that opts out of the shell still opts into the system.
nodes.rationale: A single off-system page (different fonts, no logo, its own palette) breaks the 'one product' feel more than any missing feature (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §23).

nodes.label: Split a product into destination pages
nodes.statement: A product is a set of destination pages (Dashboard, Components, Guide, Graph), not one endless scroll. Keep the global menu short and destination-oriented; deep section lists live on the page, not in the sidebar.
nodes.rationale: One long everything-page is a sampler, not a product — it buries the hierarchy and the way around (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §22).

nodes.label: Buttons are pills (radius-full)
nodes.statement: Buttons use the fully-rounded pill radius — the 2one signature. Do not square them off.
nodes.rationale: The pill is the single most recognisable 2one form cue.

nodes.label: All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.statement: Every transition/animation must be disabled or reduced under prefers-reduced-motion. Motion is purposeful (opacity/transform), never decorative.
nodes.rationale: Motion can trigger vestibular disorders; it must be opt-out-able by the OS setting.

nodes.label: Tailwind only keeps classes it can SEE
nodes.statement: @source every folder you render. An arbitrary value (h-[250px]) used in exactly one place is the canary — if it does nothing, the folder was never scanned.
nodes.rationale: A class in an un-scanned folder is never generated at all.

nodes.label: Theme via ThemeProvider — light + audited dark
nodes.statement: Switch themes with the exported ThemeProvider (light + audited dark). Never hand-roll a third palette, a brand hue, or data-* dark hacks.
nodes.rationale: Both shipped themes are APCA-audited; a hand-rolled palette bypasses the audit.

nodes.label: Theme only through tokens — no hard-coded hex or second palette
nodes.statement: Every colour comes from a DLS token. No hard-coded hex, no parallel palette.
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded colour drifts from the tokens and breaks recolour + theming.

nodes.label: Never put essential information only in a Tooltip
nodes.statement: Tooltips are supplementary. Any information the user MUST perceive to succeed (required, error, or instruction) must be visible without hover or focus discovery — not tooltip-only.
nodes.rationale: Tooltips are unreachable on touch and are skipped by many assistive contexts; essential info behind one is lost.

nodes.label: danger/success for validation only
nodes.statement: Use danger and success colours only to express validation state (error/success) — never for emphasis, branding, or decoration.
nodes.rationale: Reserving the only two hues for state keeps their meaning unambiguous.

nodes.label: Cap width by content type
nodes.statement: A reading-width cap is for long-form prose only. App/component layouts get a generous responsive cap (max-w-7xl) or go fluid; cap only the prose inside.
nodes.rationale: A reading cap on an app wastes half a large monitor in empty gutters.

nodes.label: Destructive Button
nodes.description: Button variant=destructive — validation/destructive only.

nodes.label: Ghost Button
nodes.description: Button variant=ghost — lowest emphasis.

nodes.label: Link Button
nodes.description: Button variant=link.

nodes.label: Outline Button
nodes.description: Button variant=outline.

nodes.label: Primary Button
nodes.description: Button variant=default — the one solid primary action.

nodes.label: Secondary Button
nodes.description: Button variant=secondary.
